corrected_value.title: Intertrial target-feature changes do not lead to more distraction by singletons: Target uncertainty does.

decisions.location: Results (Experiment 1, Intertrial analysis of target features), lines 432-437; References, lines 881-885
decisions.quote:
Furthermore, RTs were shorter when the target shape was repeated
than when it changed (881 vs. 915 ms), F(1, 31) ⫽ 21.18, p ⬍
.001, ␩p2 ⫽ 0.406, but there was no interaction with distractor
presence (p ⫽ .505), confirming that repetition of the task-relevant
shape feature did not affect interference from the distractor (Lamy
& Yashar, 2008).
decisions.reason: In Experiment 1 Results (lines 422-437), the authors test whether repeating vs. changing the task-relevant target shape modulates interference from the salient distractor when distractor presence is randomly varied (test phase), finding a main effect of target shape repetition (881 vs. 915 ms, F(1, 31) = 21.18, p < .001) with no distractor-presence interaction (p = .505), and explicitly state this confirms that repetition of the task-relevant shape feature did not affect interference from the distractor (Lamy & Yashar, 2008). The only shipped row for this source work (input_row_index 2132) is Leber & Egeth (2006, 10.3758/bf03193824), which is a different paper and effect. Therefore, Lamy & Yashar (2008) is a genuinely absent replication-original pair.
